pr_body:
* Extracted from #79366 for easier review.

Replace `_property_info_from_datatype()` with `_doctype_from_gdtype()` to get the type info more universally, without intermediate conversion to `PropertyInfo`/`MethodInfo` using `DocData`'s static methods, since this has issues with custom types.

* Closes #67704.
  * Adds default values of argument and properties (or `<unknown>` if the value is not a constant expression).
* Closes #79247.
* Closes #80734.
* Use only hard types, show `Variant` instead of inferred weak type.
* Add `static` qualifier to static methods.

CC @anvilfolk

issue_context.title: In Custom Class Documentation a Function cannot return 'Variant'
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.1.1.stable.official [bd6af8e0e]

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

As said in the Title Custom Class Documentation a Function cannot return 'Variant' and will instead be shown to return void, even though Built-in Classes are shown to return 'Variant', an example would be 'Array'
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/34311843/fb8ad532-c37a-43c0-a95f-d70af7ea6894)
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/34311843/3cc1e07b-02e1-4f33-bc98-0fa016b4d864)

### Steps to reproduce

```gdscript
extends Node
class_name CustomClass

func VariantFunction() -> Variant:
	return 10
``` 
Now when checking the Generated Documentation it will appear like: `void VariantFunction()`

### Minimal reproduction project

N/A

review_comments:
`r_type` and `r_enum` means that the arguments must be the `type` (or `return_type`) and `enumeration` (or `return_enum`) properties of `DocData` structures. This is consistent with `EditorHelp::_add_type()` (just GDScript doesn't support `BitField`). `r_enum` cannot contain information about the element type of a typed array.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5444afae63f37cb4b890c781e5679a3b7ee5a392/editor/editor_help.h#L161

I think I got confused with this line though:

`r_enum += "[]";`

which makes it seem like something is happening with arrays. I guess this is just handling for an array of enums then?

Yes, this is a bit of a non-obvious thing. It's because of the following code:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5444afae63f37cb4b890c781e5679a3b7ee5a392/editor/editor_help.cpp#L316-L323

I think I see. Although won't the `link_t` itself then be `enum_name[]`, which might not work? Do we need to trim the `[]` from the end, perhaps?

I was pretty sleep when I wrote that code, so feel free to change it if you find that it makes more sense some other way! :)

This is an interesting question as it affects XML docs.

```
SomeEnum    -> type="int" enum="SomeEnum"
Node        -> type="Node"
Array       -> type="Array"
Array[Node] -> type="Node[]" // Not `type="Array" elem_type="Node"`.
```

I'm not sure which `Array[SomeEnum]` should be according to the logic:

1. `type="SomeEnum[]" enum=""`
2. `type="Array" enum="SomeEnum[]"`
3. `type="int[]" enum="SomeEnum[]"`

But I tested, Option 2 works in Editor Help. Option 3 should also work (the `type` doesn't matter if `enum` is specified). Option 3 is probably the most correct:

```gdscript
enum SomeEnum {}
var a: Array[SomeEnum]

func _run() -> void:
    print(a.get_typed_builtin() == TYPE_INT) # true
    print(a.get_typed_class_name()) # (empty string)
    print(a.get_typed_script()) # <Object#null>
```

Sounds reasonable, but I don't think it will work because of the hard type check at the beginning of the function. In addition, we do not have an agreement on what should be returned in case of type resolution error, we often return `VARIANT` dummy type.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5444afae63f37cb4b890c781e5679a3b7ee5a392/modules/gdscript/gdscript_analyzer.cpp#L3874-L3876

Note: `DataType::to_string()` uses `<unresolved type>`.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5444afae63f37cb4b890c781e5679a3b7ee5a392/modules/gdscript/gdscript_parser.cpp#L4324-L4326

We would probably also have to change `EditorHelp` around so it would support compilation error formatting, so we can leave it as is, since it's the way it's always been, and consider this for a future PR?
I'm not sure if we should be worried about this, it's unlikely that users will check compilation errors with the documentation rather than with the Debugger/Errors panel.

This feels OK, but there are a few other paths where scripts could, in theory, be taken from, like `usr://` or whatever the path for that is. I don't think it's an issue, and this being a little more restrictive also feels a little safer :)

I think that if some other protocol is supported, then shortening its path might lead to collisions:

```
res://script.gd -> "script.gd"
user://script.gd -> "script.gd"
```

If we shorten only the `res://`, there will be no collision:

```
res://script.gd -> "script.gd"
user://script.gd -> "user://script.gd"
```

Oh, I think I see what you are saying! Right now there might be collisions but after this PR there shouldn't. We just assume the default is from `res://`. Anything that isn't from there will have an explicit prefix. I like it! 👍

Could we say `<not constant>` here instead? At least it explains why a specific value is not known.

I just copied this from function signature hint. If we want to change this, then we need to do it here as well:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5444afae63f37cb4b890c781e5679a3b7ee5a392/modules/gdscript/gdscript_editor.cpp#L720-L722

More options: `<non-constant>`, `<non-const-expr>`, `<dynamic>`, `<unresolved>`.

I personally really like `<non-const-expr>` for some reason! I just feel like it's worth explaining _why_ something is unknown, as opposed to just stating that it is. That way people can more easily and immediately understand what's happening.

I don't think changing `gdscript_editor.cpp` would lead to significant compat breaking, right?
It's a bit ugly in my opinion because of the two hyphens and longer text. I would choose `<unknown>`, `<dynamic>` or `<non-constant>`.

I see your own, and my opinion is certainly very subjective. I don't think `<unknown>` captures the reason why a value can't be written. I think `<dynamic>` hints at it but isn't the most explicit, whereas `<non-constant>` is the clearest to me, though I agree it isn't the prettiest.
Let's keep `<unknown>` for now since we haven't reached a consensus and there is a precedent with signature hint. We can fix this later or maybe some other reviewer will give their opinion.
